properties.natural_language: All data received via Node operator provides weak subjectivity checkpoint from EXT-NODE-OPERATOR must be validated before processing. Checkpoint must be validated against known chain state. Must be within weak subjectivity period. Invalid checkpoint enables long-range attacks and syncing to invalid chain.
If input from EXT-NODE-OPERATOR via Node operator provides weak subjectivity checkpoint fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.

All data received via Begin checkpoint validation from EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P must be validated before processing. Full block validation required: header fields, gas limit bounds, PoW/PoS validity, transaction execution correctness, state root verification. All data from peers is potentially malicious.
If input from EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P via Begin checkpoint validation fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
After Validate Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint completes, the system must transition to Checkpoint Validated with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint completes, the system must transition to Checkpoint Invalid with all state invariants preserved.
Before Synchronize From Checkpoint can execute, the system must be in Checkpoint Validated.
After Synchronize From Checkpoint completes, the system must transition to Client Synchronized with all state invariants preserved.
While in Client Uninitialized: New execution client has no blockchain state and needs to synchronize.

All data received via Peer transmits block via devp2p from EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P must be validated before processing. Full block header and body validation required: block number, timestamp, gas limit, gas used, extra data, parent hash, difficulty (pre-merge), PoW (pre-merge). All data from peers is potentially malicious.
If input from EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P via Peer transmits block via devp2p fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.

All data received via Peer requests historical block data via devp2p from EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P must be validated before processing. Requests must be bounded by HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS window. Resource exhaustion prevention required for serving peers.
If input from EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P via Peer requests historical block data via devp2p fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.

All data received via Begin data integrity verification from EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P must be validated before processing. Full block validation required: header fields, gas limit bounds, PoW/PoS validity, transaction execution correctness, state root verification. All data from peers is potentially malicious.
If input from EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P via Begin data integrity verification fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Data from external entity EXT-DAPP via dApp requests historical data older than 1 year must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Data from external entity EXT-DATA-PROVIDER via External source returns historical data must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Query External Data Source can execute, the system must be in Historical Data Needed.
After Validate External Data completes, the system must transition to External Data Validated with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate External Data completes, the system must transition to External Data Invalid with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP4444-01): Clients SHOULD NOT serve headers, block bodies, and receipts that are older than HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS — the system must enforce: Assume SHOULD NOT as a soft requirement - clients MAY still serve old data but are not obligated. For security modeling, assume most clients will NOT serve old data after adoption.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP4444-02): The specification does not define how to validate historical data obtained from out-of-band sources — the system must enforce: Assume validation requires checking data against known state roots or accumulator proofs. This is a critical security gap to address.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP4444-03): The weak subjectivity period must never exceed the history prune epoch threshold - relationship not precisely defined — the system must enforce: Assume that HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS (82,125 epochs) must always be greater than the weak subjectivity period to ensure checkpoint data is available.

The system assumes: Node operators are assumed to provide valid weak subjectivity checkpoints to their clients. If violated: Malicious or compromised checkpoint could lead to client syncing to an invalid chain state, enabling long-range attacks

The system assumes: Out-of-band historical data sources (IPFS, Portal Network, indexers) will remain available and provide authentic data. If violated: Historical data could become unavailable or corrupted, breaking dApps dependent on old blockchain data

The system assumes: Organizations will voluntarily maintain and distribute historical blockchain data via alternative channels. If violated: Historical data centralization risk - few entities controlling access to old blockchain data

The system assumes: External historical data providers (The Graph, indexing services) can be trusted to serve authentic data. If violated: Centralized data providers could serve falsified historical data to dependent applications

Despite ambiguity (AMB-PRAGUE-STACK-01): The behavior of DUP and SWAP operations with respect to stack limits is not detailed in this module — the system must enforce: Assume DUP operations check for overflow (net +1) and SWAP operations check for sufficient depth but no overflow (net 0).
The system assumes: The stack limit of 1024 is enforced at the list level, not by memory allocation. If violated: Memory exhaustion attacks could occur if implementation allows larger stacks
The system assumes: Stack operations are atomic and cannot be interrupted mid-operation. If violated: Partial stack modifications could leave EVM in inconsistent state
The system assumes: All U256 values on the stack are within valid 256-bit bounds. If violated: Invalid stack values could cause undefined behavior in arithmetic operations

Despite ambiguity (AMB-CONSTANTINOPLE-01): The specification does not explicitly enumerate which EIPs are included in Constantinople — the system must enforce: Assume Constantinople includes EIP-145 (bitwise shifting), EIP-1014 (CREATE2), EIP-1052 (EXTCODEHASH), EIP-1283 (SSTORE metering). This needs cross-reference with EIP meta.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-CONSTANTINOPLE-02): The ommer adjustment multiplier of 1 or 2 is mentioned without clear conditions — the system must enforce: Assume multiplier is 2 if ommers are present in the block, 1 otherwise. This affects difficulty adjustment timing.

The system assumes: The Ethash cache generation is assumed to be deterministic and reproducible across all nodes. If violated: Non-deterministic cache would cause different PoW validation results, breaking consensus
The system assumes: The 50% gas refund cap prevents abuse of SSTORE refund mechanism. If violated: Unlimited refunds could enable economic attacks or unexpected gas dynamics

The system assumes: The 5,000,000 block difficulty bomb delay constant is correctly applied at Constantinople activation. If violated: Incorrect bomb delay would cause unexpected difficulty spikes or drops
The system assumes: All 255 recent block hashes are available for BLOCKHASH opcode. If violated: Missing historical hashes could break contracts relying on BLOCKHASH for randomness

Despite ambiguity (AMB-RELEASE-01): The release workflow 'can take up to 24 hours' without specifying what determines the duration. — the system must enforce: Assume duration depends on reference test generation and artifact compilation. The 24-hour upper bound is a practical observation, not a hard limit.

The system assumes: Repository maintainers who merge VERSION.txt changes and publish releases are trusted to not introduce malicious specification changes.. If violated: Compromised maintainer could publish specifications with subtle security flaws that client teams would implement, affecting the entire network.

The system assumes: GitHub Actions infrastructure is available and uncompromised for workflow execution.. If violated: Compromised CI could inject malicious reference tests, leading client implementations to adopt incorrect behavior.

All data received via Proof delivered asynchronously via beacon API from EXT-PROOF-ENGINE must be validated before processing. Proof engine output crosses a trust boundary. Prover must validate proof content before signing with BLS. Domain separation via DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF prevents cross-domain replay. Invalid proofs from a compromised engine could deceive stateless validators if signed by a whitelisted prover.
If input from EXT-PROOF-ENGINE via Proof delivered asynchronously via beacon API fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.

After Request Proof Generation completes, the system must transition to Proof Generation In Progress with all state invariants preserved.

After Verify Execution Proof completes, the system must transition to Execution Proof Invalid with all state invariants preserved.

All data received via Proof delivered to beacon API endpoint from EXT-PROOF-PROVIDER-P2P must be validated before processing. Proof must be verified against a trusted root. Proof length must match generalized index depth. Reconstructed root must exactly equal expected root. SHA-256 collision resistance is assumed.
If input from EXT-PROOF-PROVIDER-P2P via Proof delivered to beacon API endpoint fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Data from external entity EXT-PROVER via External prover delivers proof via API must be treated as untrusted and validated.
After Receive Proof via Beacon API completes, Validate Proof Format and Type must proceed as specified by: Check proof matches expected types.
After Validate Proof Format and Type completes, the system must transition to Proof Stored in ProofState with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP8025-01): Validation functions are 'implementation dependent' with no specified behavior — the system must enforce: Assume each implementation must provide cryptographic proof verification that ensures execution validity. The interface contract (boolean return) is the only guaranteed behavior.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP8025-02): No specification of what happens if proof delivery times out or is never received — the system must enforce: Assume the system must handle timeout cases; likely falls back to full execution validation or rejects the payload.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP8025-03): ProofType is referenced but not enumerated; unclear what proof types exist — the system must enforce: Assume ProofType is an extensible enum defined elsewhere; the proof engine must support all types listed in ProofAttributes.

The system assumes: The external proof engine is trusted to generate correct proofs; the consensus layer only verifies, it does not generate proofs itself. If violated: A compromised proof engine could generate false proofs, allowing invalid execution payloads to be accepted

The system assumes: The beacon API endpoint POST /eth/v1/prover/execution_proofs is only accessible to authorized proof engines. If violated: An attacker could submit forged proofs via the API endpoint, bypassing execution validation

The system assumes: Proof generation completes within a reasonable time bound relative to slot duration. If violated: Delayed proof delivery could cause missed slots or force fallback to full execution

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2935-01): The system call 'does not count against the block's gas limit' — the system must enforce: Assume the system call gas is entirely separate from block gas accounting, but normal EVM rules (like SSTORE costs) still apply within the call.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2935-02): HISTORY_SERVE_WINDOW is 8,191 blocks, but the reason for this specific number is not explained — the system must enforce: Assume 8,191 is chosen as a prime number to ensure good hash distribution in the ring buffer and avoid aliasing patterns.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2935-03): Behavior when SYSTEM_ADDRESS already has a balance is not specified — the system must enforce: Assume SYSTEM_ADDRESS is a reserved address that cannot normally receive ETH and any existing balance is irrelevant to the system call.

The system assumes: The SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xff..fe) cannot be controlled by any external entity. If violated: If SYSTEM_ADDRESS could be controlled, attacker could write arbitrary hashes, breaking the chain's integrity
The system assumes: Block hashes are cryptographically collision-resistant. If violated: Hash collisions could allow attackers to substitute blocks or confuse contracts relying on hash verification
The system assumes: All clients implement the system call at exactly the same point in block processing. If violated: Inconsistent implementation could cause consensus failures between clients
The system assumes: Attackers cannot manipulate block numbers to access hashes outside the intended window. If violated: Could allow unauthorized access to stale or invalid hash data

The system assumes: The ring buffer will be fully populated after 8,191 blocks post-activation. If violated: Early blocks after activation may have undefined slots that could return zero or revert unpredictably

All data received via Call to predeploy contract from EXT-USER-JSON-RPC must be validated before processing. All RPC method calls must be validated. Reserved rpc.* namespace must be enforced.
If input from EXT-USER-JSON-RPC via Call to predeploy contract fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7002-01): The specification states 'exact fees cannot be predetermined' but does not specify the maximum time between fee query and transaction inclusion. — the system must enforce: Assume smart contracts should query fees in the same transaction as submission (via static call) and implement slippage protection with a maximum fee parameter.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7002-02): The EIP does not specify behavior when the predeploy contract is called with calldata between 0 and 56 bytes (exclusive). — the system must enforce: Assume any calldata that is not exactly 0 bytes (fee query) or 56 bytes (withdrawal request) results in transaction failure or no-op.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7002-03): The term 'partial withdrawal' is used without specifying minimum or maximum amounts. — the system must enforce: Assume partial withdrawals follow existing consensus layer rules for minimum and maximum withdrawal amounts.

The system assumes: The predeploy contract at address 0x00000961Ef480Eb55e80D19ad83579A64c007002 is correctly deployed and immutable.. If violated: Block validation fails, potential chain halt or fork if contract is missing or corrupted at activation.

The system assumes: Existing custody arrangements relying on withdrawal credentials not being able to trigger exits have been renegotiated or migrated.. If violated: Trust relationships violated, potential for unauthorized validator exits by withdrawal credential holders.

The system assumes: An attacker cannot spam withdrawal requests indefinitely due to the exponential fee mechanism.. If violated: Griefing attack possible if attacker has sufficient ETH, causing legitimate users to face prohibitive fees.

The system assumes: The consensus layer will process withdrawal requests within a bounded time, preventing indefinite queuing.. If violated: Unbounded queue growth could lead to state bloat and degraded performance.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-ELLIPTIC-CURVE-01): The specification does not explicitly define behavior when v (recovery identifier) is outside expected range [0, 1, 27, 28] — the system must enforce: Assume the coincurve library handles invalid v values and raises appropriate errors. This needs verification against library behavior.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-ELLIPTIC-CURVE-02): The term 'valid x-coordinate' in Legendre symbol validation is not precisely defined — the system must enforce: Assume 'valid' means the value x satisfies: x³ + 7 (mod p) is a quadratic residue, allowing recovery of a y-coordinate on the curve.

The system assumes: The coincurve library implementation is assumed to be cryptographically correct and secure. If violated: Incorrect ECDSA operations could allow signature forgery or public key recovery attacks

The system assumes: All arithmetic is performed modulo respective field primes, assuming no integer overflow in underlying implementation. If violated: Integer overflow could lead to incorrect curve point calculations and signature validation bypass

The system assumes: All clients will implement the fork consistently at the same FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER. If violated: Inconsistent fork activation could cause chain splits between updated and non-updated clients

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7495-01): The relationship between EIP-7495 and EIP-7916 (progressive Merkle trees) is not fully specified in terms of implementation order. — the system must enforce: Assume EIP-7916 defines the underlying progressive Merkle tree structure and EIP-7495 defines the container-level semantics built on top of it.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7495-02): The specification mentions 'max 256 bits' for active_fields but doesn't clarify handling of larger containers if needed in future. — the system must enforce: Assume 256 is a hard protocol limit and containers requiring more fields would need a different mechanism or type.

The system assumes: Verifiers trust that the active_fields bitvector accurately represents which fields are present in the container.. If violated: A forged active_fields could allow an attacker to create colliding hashes for containers with different field configurations.

The system assumes: Light clients and smart contracts have access to the correct container schema definition to interpret active_fields.. If violated: Verifiers with outdated schemas may misinterpret proofs or reject valid containers.

The system assumes: The hash function used for Merkleization (SHA256 or similar) is collision-resistant.. If violated: Hash collisions could allow attackers to forge Merkle proofs for arbitrary field values.

The system assumes: Attackers cannot manipulate the serialized representation to create valid-looking containers with forged field values.. If violated: Deserialization attacks could inject malicious field values into trusted container structures.
